dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows long-form text it did not lay out by hand — a help article, release notes, legal terms, a message written in Markdown, content from a CMS — and wants its headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes to read as one text with one rhythm, at the text size of the interface in a panel and at a reading size on a page of its own.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything prose reads: per size, the text style of running text and of secondary text; the lead paragraph's text style; the longest line, as a number of ems of the running text; the space between blocks, between list items and between blocks nested in an item or a quote; the space before and after each heading level; the inset of list items; a quote's line and inset; the space around a rule; the space before a heading's anchor; and the size of a task item's mark. Headings take sys.typescale.heading-1 to heading-6 directly: the roles are named for the levels.
rules: Prose styles text you did not lay out by hand (rendered Markdown, CMS content). Text you place yourself takes a text style of sys.typescale directly.
Pick a heading's level by the document's structure, never by the size you want; re-value the role in a layer instead.
Tanrei does not parse Markdown or HTML on any platform: your renderer produces the blocks, prose styles and spaces them.
A component placed inside prose (a code block, a table, a callout, a figure) is spaced by prose and styled by itself; do not restyle its inside from prose.
To change the rhythm, re-point these tokens in a layer; never add margins by hand.
Use size large for a page whose purpose is reading; medium where prose sits among controls (a panel, a dialog, a card).

measure.$description: The longest line of a text block, as a multiple of the running text's font size (ems): 36 full-width characters of Japanese or Chinese, about 72 to 80 of Latin text. A text block is never wider; a block that is not text (a table, a code block, a figure) is not limited by it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product limits how long a line of reading text grows on a wide window, apart from how wide its tables, code and pictures may be, because a line that is too long loses the reader on the way back.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A count of characters, not a distance: it scales with the running text's size by being multiplied by it, and no dial moves it.

typescale.$description: Running text, per size: paragraphs, list items, a quote's text, a description.
Secondary text, per size: `small`, footnotes. One body role below the running text.

A lead paragraph: the one paragraph, marked by the author, that introduces the text. The same at both sizes: at large the running text already is this role, and the lead is then told apart by nothing (no larger body role exists in the core).

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product opens an article with a standfirst set a step above its running text.

gap.$description: Space between two blocks that follow each other: paragraphs, lists, quotes, and any component placed in the flow.
Space between the items of a list, between an item's text and a list nested in it, and between a term and its description.

Space between blocks inside a list item or a quote, between the items of a list whose items hold more than one block, and between the groups of a description list. Smaller than block.gap, so what is nested reads as one unit.

indent.$description: How far a list's items are set in from the list's start edge, at every depth; the marker hangs in this space. Also the inset of a description. Wide enough for a two-digit number and its period at both sizes.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product aligns what is set in from the text's edge — list items, descriptions — at one distance, chosen so its numbered lists' markers fit.

before.$description: Space above a level 1 heading, when something precedes it in the same flow. Larger than block.gap, so the heading belongs to what follows it.

after.$description: Space between a level 1 heading and the block that follows it — also when that block is another heading. Never larger than block.gap.

before.$description: Space above a level 2 heading, when something precedes it in the same flow. Larger than block.gap, so the heading belongs to what follows it.

after.$description: Space between a level 2 heading and the block that follows it — also when that block is another heading. Never larger than block.gap.

before.$description: Space above a level 3 heading, when something precedes it in the same flow. Larger than block.gap, so the heading belongs to what follows it.

after.$description: Space between a level 3 heading and the block that follows it — also when that block is another heading. Never larger than block.gap.

before.$description: Space above a level 4 heading, when something precedes it in the same flow. Larger than block.gap, so the heading belongs to what follows it.

after.$description: Space between a level 4 heading and the block that follows it — also when that block is another heading. Never larger than block.gap.

before.$description: Space above a level 5 heading, when something precedes it in the same flow. Larger than block.gap, so the heading belongs to what follows it.

after.$description: Space between a level 5 heading and the block that follows it — also when that block is another heading. Never larger than block.gap.

before.$description: Space above a level 6 heading, when something precedes it in the same flow. Larger than block.gap, so the heading belongs to what follows it.

after.$description: Space between a level 6 heading and the block that follows it — also when that block is another heading. Never larger than block.gap.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product sets quoted text apart from its own words by a line along its edge, quieter than a container and without changing the text.

color.$description: The line along a quote's start edge: the system's one hairline color. Decorative: the quote is exposed as a quote without it.

thickness.$description: The line's width. Heavier than a hairline, so it reads as a mark and not as a container's edge.

inset.$description: Space between the line and the quote's content.

gap.$description: Space above and below a rule (a thematic break). The rule itself is the divider, drawn from the divider's tokens.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product breaks a long text into parts without a heading, and gives that break the room a new section gets.

gap.$description: Space between the end of a heading's text and its anchor link.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product lets people copy a link to a section of a long page; the link sits after the heading's text.

size.$description: The mark of a task item (done or not done), drawn in place of the list marker from the system's icon set.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows a checklist inside its text — release notes, a migration guide — whose items are read, not pressed.
